chain.label: Helicopter Route 4 charted with no lateral boundaries or defined offset from the shoreline
chain.trigger: helicopter routes have no defined lateral boundaries and are drawn to depict linear paths along defined surface features

chain.label: Route 4 corridor overlaps the runway 33 final approach path, leaving about 75 ft or less vertical separation
chain.trigger: existing separation distances between helicopter traffic operating on Route 4 and aircraft landing on runway 33 are insufficient and pose an intolerable risk

caused_by.evidence: the Baltimore-Washington Helicopter Route Chart includes no warning for helicopters to operate a defined distance from the shoreline... this distance decreases if the helicopter is operated farther from the shoreline

chain.label: Night conditions; helicopter crew operating on a night vision goggle evaluation flight
chain.trigger: annual standardization evaluation with the use of night vision goggles. Night visual meteorological conditions prevailed

chain.label: Controller placed flight 5342 on a runway 33 approach while PAT25 transited Route 4 southbound, converging the two aircraft
chain.trigger: The controller asked the crew of flight 5342 if they could accept runway 33 for landing, and the flight crew accepted. At this time, PAT25 was traveling south along the Potomac River and flight 5342 was traveling north.

caused_by.evidence: Conducting northbound operations with simultaneous operations to runways 1 and 33 is a routine ATC procedure

chain.label: Helicopter at about 300 ft in a Route 4 segment with a 200-ft msl maximum altitude
chain.trigger: The collision occurred at 2047:59, at an altitude about 300 ft

caused_by.evidence: Two-thirds of the events occurred at night... In over half of these instances, the helicopter may have been above the route altitude restriction.

chain.label: PAT25 crew reported the CRJ in sight and accepted visual separation but did not maintain separation from flight 5342
chain.trigger: PAT25 immediately confirmed that the traffic was in sight and again requested visual separation

caused_by.evidence: Night visual meteorological conditions prevailed in the area of DCA at the time of the accident.
the controller advised PAT25 that traffic just south of the Wilson Bridge was a CRJ (flight 5342) at 1,200 ft circling to runway 33

chain.label: Controller re-approved visual separation after the tower conflict alert instead of issuing positive separation instructions
chain.trigger: An aural conflict alert in the tower can be heard in the background of the ATC recording at this time... again requested visual separation, which the controller approved

caused_by.evidence: the controller instructed PAT25 to pass behind the CRJ; PAT25 immediately confirmed that the traffic was in sight

chain.label: UH-60L and CL-600-2C10 collided on short final to runway 33
chain.trigger: collided in flight about 0.5 nautical miles (nm) southeast of runway 33

caused_by.evidence: preliminary findings suggest that the existing separation distances between helicopter traffic operating on Route 4 and aircraft landing on runway 33 are insufficient
The collision occurred at 2047:59, at an altitude about 300 ft
PAT25 confirmed 7 seconds later that they had the traffic in sight and requested visual separation, which the controller approved
About 4 seconds later, the controller instructed PAT25 to pass behind the CRJ

chain.label: Both aircraft impacted the Potomac River and were destroyed
chain.trigger: impacted the Potomac River in southwest Washington, DC

caused_by.evidence: Both aircraft were destroyed as a result of the accident.

chain.label: All 67 aboard both aircraft fatally injured
chain.trigger: The 2 pilots, 2 flight attendants, and 60 passengers aboard the airplane and all 3 crewmembers aboard the helicopter were fatally injured.
